_note: Phase 4 finale: final assembly gate, the in-engine escape cinematic, the mission report, the scoring formula and the credits. All timings are seconds of cinematic time; all prose is here, not in scripts. Every number and claim about the ship comes from the player's own recorded run. Time travel, the portal and the VELA drive are fictional story devices.

assembly.subtitle: VELA / return mission
steps: Survey the frozen design against the recovered frame.

cinematic.title: ESCAPE
cinematic.skip_hint: ESC SKIP   SPACE PAUSE   ANY KEY NEXT

flight._note: Tuning for the two playable flight segments. VELA flies upright: `x` (ship_x, spawn_x, portal_x) is the along-track axis and runs up the screen (screen y = 360 - x); `y` (lane_top/bottom, portal_y) is the across-track axis, screen x, the axis the player steers on. ship_half_length and the shield half-extents match the canonical VELA renderer at scale 1 (core/star_fall/sf_vela.gd). `target_seconds` is how long a clean run of the segment takes; the assist values guarantee that a player who never touches the controls, or who keeps colliding, still finishes. Grit is small debris aimed at the ship and absorbed by the shield; graze_push is how hard the shield shoves a large body that passes close. The portal captures the ship after align_seconds in the mouth and then flies it in (entry_start_speed, entry_accel); the scene only moves on after the hull has crossed. `kind` is the only field the screen dispatches on.

lines.text: Nick and Bill stand beside the repaired VELA on the crash-site pad.
Bill's memory core streams into the ship through the service terminal.
Bill: "That is the last of the old body. It did its job."
Nick: "So did you."
The junction you bridged still carries power to the pad.
Nick climbs aboard and seals the hatch. Departure checks complete.
The rebuilt drive catches on the first attempt.
Smoke pours off the pad. VELA lifts straight up out of the wreck field.
The shield emitter lights: a blue bubble around the hull.
The junk strata thicken with altitude. Every contact ripples the shield.
The last shell thins out. The shield held every contact.
Bill: "Meteoroids. Steer with A and D, or move the mouse."
Nick: "I have it. Keeping to the gaps."
Bill: "The shield takes the grit. A big one on the hull puts us back at the start."
Nick: "Then let's not get hit."
Bill: "Small hits only. Keep her steady."
The passage opens. The lane goes quiet.
Below, the old world is smothered in its own waste.
Bill: "Is the sky still blue where you come from?"
Nick: "It is."
Bill: "Then keep it that way."
The cabin goes quiet. The light does not.
VELA replays the original recorded signal. Something answers.
Bill: "There it is. Line up under the opening and hold. It will pull us in."
Nick: "Aligning. Hold it steady."
The access window is open. This is the story's way home, not a claim about physics.
Mission Control: "VELA, we have your signal. What happened?"
Nick: "I have data to send. This time, we need to listen."
Engines off. The pad is real, and the grass is green.
The ramp comes down. Nick steps out onto present-day Earth.
The archive opens: the memories you found, in the order you found them.
The records reach researchers, analysts and the coastal communities.
Not one person solves it. The information is finally where it can be used.
Nick: "Bill... it is still blue."

lines: You found your way back to Earth.
Help keep it a home for those who come after us.

report.title: MISSION REPORT
report.subtitle: Compiled from the recorded run

labels.built: Built at the spaceport on day one
labels.skipped: Cinematic skipped. This has no effect on the outcome or the score.

report.efficiency_note: dry mass in kg per salvage unit spent (materials + fabrication units)

decisions.repair_original: You repaired the day-one engine rather than rebuilding one: fewer fabrication units and less margin spent on hardware.
decisions.rebuilt_cluster: You rebuilt a Dawn cluster: more thrust and efficiency, paid for in fabrication units.
decisions.protection_none: You trusted the shield emitter alone and spent the saved mass on propellant.
decisions.armor_plating: You fitted scrap armor: physical protection bought with mass, and mass bought with propellant.
decisions.shield_amplifier: You fitted the shield amplifier: protection bought with electrical load during the transit.
decisions.storage_none: You relied on the navigation chip's own store.
decisions.storage_compact: You chose the compact data module: enough room for the evidence with little extra load.
decisions.storage_array: You fitted the archive array: more room for records, more mass and more power draw.
decisions.fast_corridor: You took the Fast Corridor: the shortest transit, against a denser debris field and a tight relay window.
decisions.extended_arc: You took the Extended Arc: less delta-v and lighter debris, paid for in hours of electrical load.
decisions.samples: You carried the environmental samples home. The cooling cost had to fit the power budget.
decisions.records: You carried the additional scientific records home. The relay window had to be long enough to sync them.
decisions.reserve: The simulation left %s of propellant and %s of buffer energy in reserve.

score._note: Published formula: 100 for completing the return objective, 25 per recovered component fitted, 15 per archived memory, 20 for flying the optional environmental samples, 20 for flying the optional additional records, plus up to 30 efficiency points computed from the simulated propellant reserve fraction. Skipping cinematics and accessibility settings never change it. Inventory size is never scored, so farming cannot raise it.

credits.title: CREDITS

sections.heading: STAR FALL
lines: A single-player pixel-art adventure.
Nick, Bill and the VELA are fictional.
Time travel, the portal and the drive are story devices.

sections.heading: ENGINE AND TOOLS
lines: Godot 4.0 stable (MIT License).
GDScript. No third-party runtime libraries.
All sprites, fonts and UI drawn procedurally at runtime.
Music and sound effects generated by the project's own Python tools.

sections.heading: ORIGINAL ASSETS
lines: Pixel font, sprites, palettes, UI and audio: original work in this repository.
No NASA imagery, logos or datasets are included.
No NASA endorsement is implied.

sections.heading: SCIENCE NOTES
lines: The rocket equation and the unit definitions are real physics.
The rocket equation is used to explain, not to simulate a real vehicle.
Component masses, costs, routes, delta-v and power budgets are invented gameplay values.
Environmental and debris statistics in the story are fictional.
No climate statistic is presented as measured data.

sections.heading: WRITING
lines: Dialogue, archives, memories and records written for this project.
Nick is human. Bill is a maintenance robot first met in the future.
The Dawn Project archive is fiction.

sections.heading: THANKS
lines: To everyone who plays carefully and asks why.

final_message: You found your way back to Earth.
Help keep it a home for those who come after us.
